title: Merging Strategies & Conflict Resolution
description: Combine lines of development with fast-forward and three-way merges, decipher conflict markers, and resolve collisions cleanly.

blocks.content: Two people changed the same sentence in different ways. You need to combine the work and make one deliberate choice. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A merge combines histories. A conflict means Git found two competing edits it cannot choose between; you edit the file, stage the resolved version, then commit.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: What does a conflict mean?
options: Git needs your decision between competing edits
blocks.explanation: Git stops because only you can decide how the competing changes should combine.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `mergeFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
keeps an already staged file while adding another
